sections.h2: What are my options for a fast sale in Lower Makefield Township?
sections.html:
Lower Makefield Township sellers can list with an agent, sell privately, or take a cash offer, and a cash sale is the shortest path because the closing date follows your calendar instead of a buyer's mortgage approval. The township's own sale steps are light: a moving permit, a sewer lateral inspection by the seller, and clean tax and utility balances.

Bucks County homes in this part of the Delaware Valley carry high values, so even a modest delay costs real carrying money in taxes, insurance and utilities. People who want a quick sale here usually have a reason beyond price: an estate that needs to be settled, a relocation, a divorce, a rental that has become a burden, or deferred repairs on a house that no longer fits the owner's plans.

  • Cash purchase: the buyer takes the house in its present condition and you set the closing date.
  • Agent listing: more exposure and often a higher price, with showings, repairs and a longer timeline.
  • For-sale-by-owner: you keep the commission money but handle marketing, contracts and negotiation yourself.

sections.h2: What should I know about Lower Makefield Township before I sell?
sections.html:
The township covers about 18.3 square miles in Bucks County along the Delaware River, facing New Jersey across the water. It wraps around the borough of Yardley on the north, south and west, which is why most addresses carry a Yardley mailing label even though they are in Lower Makefield. Across the river are Hopewell Township, Ewing Township and Trenton, and on the Pennsylvania side the neighbors are Upper Makefield, Newtown, Middletown and Falls townships plus Morrisville.

Brock Creek, Common Creek, Core Creek and Jericho Creek run through it, and Edge Hill is a named local landform. Past and present villages include Schammels Corner and Woodside. The population rose from 25,083 in 1990 to 32,681 in 2000, and later office growth centered on the Stony Hill Road corridor near Interstate 295. Children attend the Pennsbury School District.

Interstate 295 is the main highway and crosses the Delaware on the Scudder Falls Bridge into New Jersey. PA Route 32 follows River Road along the water, PA Route 332 follows Newtown-Yardley Road through the middle, and US Route 1 clips the southern corner. As of 2018, 175.27 miles of public road ran through the township, and 138.20 miles of that were township maintained. SEPTA bus route 127 reaches the southern tip. The West Trenton regional rail line passes through the township without a station inside it, so commuters use Yardley station or Woodbourne station in Middletown Township. The area sits in hardiness zone 7a, so a buyer's inspector will look at roofs, gutters and basements with winter freezes in mind.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about homes in Lower Makefield Township?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimated 34,028 residents on July 1, 2025. Of occupied housing, 87.6 percent is owner occupied, and the median value of an owner-occupied home was $630,200 over 2020 to 2024. Median gross rent was $2,340 and the median household income was $175,206 in 2024 dollars. A bachelor's degree or higher is held by 69.4 percent of adults, and 91.6 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

That profile means most sales are single-family homes where the owner lives, and values are well above most of Pennsylvania. Prices at this level make every percentage point of transfer tax and every month of carrying cost visible, so it pays to compare closing timelines as carefully as the offer price.

sections.h2: What taxes does a Lower Makefield property carry?
sections.html:
Real estate tax comes from three bills: township, county and the Pennsbury School District. The township tax collector page lists the 2025 combined rate at 256.403 mills, and the township levies no earned income tax.

2025 real estate millage on a Lower Makefield Township property, per the township tax collector
Taxing bodyMills
Lower Makefield Township24.95
Bucks County27.45
Pennsbury School District (2025-2026)204.003
Total256.403

One mill is one tenth of one percent of assessed value. Township and county bills are issued around March 1 for the calendar year, with a 2 percent discount for payment within two months, face amount within four months and a 10 percent penalty afterward. School bills are issued around July 1 for the school year. Unpaid taxes pass to the Bucks County Tax Claim Bureau after the collector's books close. When you sell, prorate these bills at settlement and ask the tax office at 267-274-1116 for current figures.

sections.h2: What does the township require when I sell?
sections.html:
The township's community development office lists three items for a sale, and it states that a resale use and occupancy certificate is not required in Lower Makefield Township. Confirm the current list with the office at 267-274-1100 before you schedule your closing, since a buyer's contract can add its own conditions.

  • A moving permit for both the buyer and the seller.
  • A sewer lateral inspection by the seller, to catch problems with the private line. Questions and submissions go to sewerlateral@lmt.org.
  • Calls to the taxing authorities and utility companies for any additional requirements they impose.

Allow time for a plumber to scope the line and for the township to review the report, since a failed line has to be fixed.

sections.h2: How does a property tax appeal work for Lower Makefield owners?
sections.html:
Bucks County sets annual appeals by a deadline in early August, and the 2026 deadline of August 3 has passed. Any change from a 2026 annual appeal takes effect in the 2027 tax year. Interim appeals follow the date printed on a recent assessment revision notice. The Board of Assessment Appeals meets on the first and third Tuesday of each month at the courthouse in Doylestown, and it can be reached at 215-348-6219.

Owner-occupants can also apply for the homestead and farmstead exclusion, which reduces the assessed value used for school tax. The county lists March 1 as the application deadline for the tax year that begins the following July 1. If you buy or sell an investment property, a Pennsylvania law added in 2026 asks owners to submit contact information to the Board within 30 days of a purchase, with owner-occupied homes excused.

sections.h2: What costs come with selling at closing?
sections.html:
The state transfer tax is 1 percent of the sale value, and the Lower Makefield Township page lists the local share as one half of one percent to the township and one half of one percent to the school district. On a $630,200 house, matching the township's median owner-occupied value, the combined 2 percent equals $12,604, split between buyer and seller by contract. Pennsylvania treats both parties as jointly responsible, so agree on who pays before signing.

Some transfers are exempt, including certain moves among family members and property passed by will or intestacy. Ask a title company to price the statement of value and recording fees at the Bucks County Recorder of Deeds, and check whether your sale involves a payoff, a lien or tenants.

faqs.q: Does Lower Makefield Township require a resale certificate?
faqs.a: The township's community development FAQ says a resale use and occupancy certificate is not required. It does require a moving permit for buyer and seller and a sewer lateral inspection by the seller, so call the township office to confirm.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax in Lower Makefield?
faqs.a: The state charges 1 percent, and the township page lists a local rate of one half percent for the township plus one half percent for the school district. That totals 2 percent of the sale price, divided by contract.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for the sewer lateral inspection?
faqs.a: The seller. The township expects the seller to inspect the private sewer line and submit the result, and its review can take time, so schedule the plumber early in your sale.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my Bucks County assessment?
faqs.a: Annual appeals are due in early August, and the 2026 deadline was August 3, so the next chance is the 2027 cycle. Interim appeals follow the date on an assessment revision notice.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Lower Makefield Township?
faqs.a: Pennsbury School District serves the township, and its 2025-2026 millage of 204.003 is the largest part of the combined 256.403 mills on a Lower Makefield tax bill.
